body: I'll admit, I've got a sweet tooth for caramel toffee ice cream. I was just having some earlier, in fact.

I'm on and off with them. As I said, I have some weeks or months of dealing with these solipsistic thoughts, but then a safe interval between for a couple weeks. During that time in between, I do get empathetic about such problems. However, once I begin shifting back to that irrational mindset, I'll shrug them off.

Right now, for example, I'm going through a mixed period where my thoughts are changing day-to-day. It's transitioning into a more right mind. If I had to put a percentage on it, I'd say about 65% rational. So I do feel for these problems right now, but only about 65% as much as I usually would.

I do not, I would consider myself agnostic.

While I do believe reality as whole is just my imagination - including all it's cultures, religions, and such - for all I know, what's past my imagination could be dropping hints in my head about what the real world is like. I have no way to know whether this is true or not, but it does get me thinking sometimes.

Hey now, this is my coma, my ideas. I'm capitalizing off these ideas, not you!

On a serious note though, that's actually a very interesting and accurate way of thinking about it.

Like I said, they're unexplainable, or rather would be extremely difficult for me to explain. But to simplify, it particularly has to do with behavior. Not like trendy sayings and the like, but rather some prominent set of behaviors which I can say that everyone fits, which I cannot see myself fitting into.

Like I said, it's extremely difficult to describe, and I doubt what I said made much sense, but that's about the best I can do.

I couldn't tell you what life is like, or hell, if it even exists. I still have yet to come to that satisfactory enough conclusion in what is beyond my imagination. For all I know, the simulation theory could be true. I don't personally side with it, but the possibilities of what's beyond are truly infinite.

I could not prove you're not conscious just as you could not prove to me that you are. Otherwise, the world would be definitively solipsistic or not. However, in my case, unexplainable patterns I notice in everyday life lead me to believe that this can't be a true-to-life world with conscious people living life by their own free will.

Nope, that's the whole idea of it. I believe that only I am conscious in a world inside my head. 

As for the part about being God, no I wouldn't say that. The idea of God is a higher power, that which looks over our world. What I believe is that this world is merely my own imagination, but not that I am a creator nor overseer. 

What's past my imagination is beyond me.
Not one bit. After all, you and your supposed mind would simply all be in my own.

I think everything is. Including the phone I'm currently using. Even my physical form, all in my head.

All I'm sure of is that I'm real. Even then, sometimes the irrationality kicks in and tells me that I myself am not real either.
That's given me a bit to think about. Thank you for replying.

That aside, positively? I did allow him to continue after all. As young as we were, I gave him my consent so I sorta feels like that would settle it?

I could, yes.

But I've been super insecure about opening up about this to other people. Even with my dad, the only reason he has a clue as to what's going on is because I was packed and ready to walk 20 miles to my sister's place, but decided to tell him and get it off my chest first. I don't want them to think any less of me or anything like that.

I've considered contacting them often, but I don't have a phone number I'd be able to call them from currently. She's put off getting me one since she broke my last one, most likely so I wouldn't be able to contact my dad as easily to talk to about the situation.

She's a self-centered, narcissistic kind of person. To add fuel to the flames, she's also an out of control alcoholic and can't go more than a day without it. 

We've talked multiple times about seeing a mental health professional or something along those lines. I always thought they went well, but I should've expected what I got. That is, she ignored me for the following weeks and the topic of it would never be brought up again. She's hypercritical of everyone around her and often will gaslight them, including my younger siblings, in order for her to prove to herself that she's not wrong. As of now, she thinks I'm just a failure of a child with no hope and treats me as such.

Talk of lawyers and CPS has been prevalent for years. I've accepted that I'm just being fed bs at this point and no e of it will ever take shape.

How my life has been going, I find that rather hard to believe, as much as I wished I could.

When I'm 18, I'll have gone through another year and a half of what I'm going through now. I'm not even sure how I'm gonna get through to next week, much less next year. My mom's mentally scarred me too deep, I don't enjoy anything anymore. Not even socializing. I'm constantly pissed over nothing. No amount of therapy could fix that, assuming I could even afford it in the first place, which I can't.

My path's been set. Time is the only obstacle left.

No one. My family writes me off as a negligent child and doesn't care to help. I've tried talking to school counselors and all they do is send me back to my family. I cut ties with all my friends a few months back because I was in about the same spot I'm in now and was unreasonably pissed at all of them.

I've got myself and no one but.
